summary: Orange County packs 3.2 million people into 800 square miles — roughly the population of Chicago spread across a landscape that runs from 42 miles of Pacific coastline up through rolling foothills and into the Santa Ana Mountains, meaning a single county contains beach towns, dense suburban corridors, and genuine canyon country with elevation gains topping 5,000 feet. That geographic range matters for daily life: average daytime highs hover around 73°F with 9.3 hours of sunshine year-round, but coastal fog and inland heat can split the county by ten degrees on any given afternoon. The employment picture is genuinely multi-industry — major employers span defense and aerospace contractors, large healthcare systems like UCI Health, theme-park operations anchored by Disneyland, and a deep bench of mid-size tech and financial firms — so switching jobs without switching commutes is more plausible here than in many Southern California bedroom communities. That said, affordability math is unforgiving: at a median household income of roughly $114K, the median home value of $915,500 produces a price-to-income ratio above 8:1, and median rent of $2,352 claims about 25 percent of gross monthly income before taxes. Property crime runs at roughly 1,780 per 100K, with motor-vehicle theft (325 per 100K) notably elevated, while violent crime sits well below national averages at 243 per 100K. Orange County's essential tension is that it offers a rare combination of economic depth, geographic beauty, and mild climate — then prices almost exactly to the point where those advantages are capitalized into every square foot of housing.
